final_candidates.decision_summary: N501Y is a well-known ACE2-affinity-enhancing RBD mutation and has high sequence-model plausibility with low toxicity risk.
Q498R is a plausible ACE2-affinity modifier with very high sequence-model plausibility and acceptable safety evidence.
S477N may enhance ACE2 binding and has moderate-to-good sequence plausibility with no concerning toxicity signal.

stop_reason.detail: All four available tool calls have been used across the candidate set.

history.rationale: Position 171 is N501 in full Spike numbering; N501Y is a well-known RBD substitution that increases ACE2 binding affinity. Strong prior for enhanced cell attachment.
No new evidence this round; retained at initial confidence because N501Y is a known ACE2-interface substitution.
Known N501Y strongly enhances ACE2 binding; moderate sequence plausibility and low toxicity are consistent, while zero evolutionary frequency is uninformative due to shallow MSA.
No new evidence this round; retained as strongest ACE2-enhancing candidate (N501Y) with high sequence plausibility.
Position 168 is Q498; Q498R has been associated with improved ACE2 interaction, especially in combination with N501Y. Plausible affinity-enhancing candidate.
No new evidence; retained as a known RBD position near the ACE2 interface.
Known Q498R ACE2-enhancing variant; high sequence plausibility and low toxicity support retention.
No new evidence this round; retained because Q498R is a plausible ACE2-affinity modifier and has high sequence plausibility.
Position 147 is S477; S477N is recurrent in variants and may enhance ACE2 binding by optimizing the binding interface. Strong prior candidate.
No new evidence; retained based on its likely ACE2-binding relevance.
Known S477N increases ACE2 affinity; lower PLM score and low MSA coverage do not outweigh established phenotype relevance.
No new evidence this round; retained as S477N may enhance ACE2 binding, with moderate sequence plausibility.
Position 122 is L452; L452R is found in multiple variants and may modestly increase ACE2 affinity while altering antibody recognition. Good candidate for binding maintenance/enhancement.
No new evidence; retained as an ACE2-adjacent position with possible binding impact.
L452R has known ACE2-enhancing effect; perfect sequence plausibility supports retention despite zero evolutionary frequency.
No new evidence this round; retained despite some uncertainty about ACE2 effect, supported by high sequence plausibility.
Position 123 is Y453; Y453F has been observed in mink-associated variants and may improve ACE2 binding. Conservative aromatic substitution with affinity potential.
No new evidence; retained for its known proximity to ACE2 contacts.
Y453F has known ACE2-enhancing effect; ideal sequence plausibility supports retention.
No new evidence this round; retained because Y453F has prior ACE2-affinity support and high sequence plausibility.
Position 148 is T478; T478K occurs in Delta/Omicron and may contribute to ACE2 interaction. Moderate prior as binding enhancer.
No new evidence; retained but requires evidence for effect direction.
T478K shows some evolutionary signal and moderate sequence plausibility, but ACE2 enhancement is modest.
No new evidence this round; retained but lowest rank due weaker ACE2-enhancement evidence despite adequate sequence plausibility.
Position 154 is E484; E484K is primarily an immune escape mutation but may retain or slightly modulate ACE2 binding. Included for evidence-based evaluation.
No new evidence; retained with moderate confidence because effect on ACE2 binding is uncertain.
E484K is known to reduce ACE2 affinity despite high sequence plausibility, making it unsuitable for this objective.

rejection.reason: E484K is known to reduce ACE2 affinity despite high sequence plausibility, making it unsuitable for this objective.

history.rationale: Position 156 is F486; substitutions here can reshape the ACE2 contact surface, with F486L plausibly maintaining or enhancing binding. Moderate prior.
No new evidence; retained with moderate confidence pending evidence.
F486L is not an established ACE2-enhancing mutation; high sequence plausibility does not override weak phenotype relevance.

rejection.reason: F486L is not an established ACE2-enhancing mutation; high sequence plausibility does not override weak phenotype relevance.

history.rationale: Position 109 is N439; N439K has been associated with increased ACE2 affinity in some variants. Reasonable candidate though less dominant than N501Y/Q498R.
No new evidence; retained as a possible ACE2-binding enhancer.
N439K is a known moderate ACE2 enhancer; improved sequence plausibility promotes it above weaker candidates.
No new evidence this round; retained as N439K is a known ACE2-affinity/immune-escape variant with moderate sequence plausibility.
Position 87 is K417; K417N is common in variants but may have context-dependent ACE2 effects. Included to test evolutionary/structure signals, lower prior for direct affinity gain.
No new evidence; retained with low confidence because its ACE2-binding direction is uncertain.
K417N is known to decrease ACE2 affinity; high sequence plausibility is misleading for this objective.

rejection.reason: K417N is known to decrease ACE2 affinity; high sequence plausibility is misleading for this objective.
